svg.text: Interactive Learning Module • No JavaScript Required

text.tspan: 1. Click any term in the Word
Bank below to highlight the
corresponding flower part.
2. Study the arrows connecting
empty slots to each structure.
3. Click "Check Answer" to reveal
all labels in their correct
positions.
4. Click "Reset" to clear and
practice again.
Flower Structure Guide:
• Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators like bees.
• Sepals are typically green and protect the flower bud before it opens.
• The Stamen is the male reproductive part, consisting of:
- Anther: Produces pollen (yellow sacs at the top)
- Filament: The thin stalk supporting the anther
• The Pistil is the female reproductive part in the center:
- Stigma: Sticky top that catches pollen
- Style: Tube connecting stigma to ovary
- Ovary: Swollen base that contains ovules (becomes fruit)
• The Receptacle is the thickened part of the stem holding all parts.
